question: A marketing lead asks Claude for a competitor briefing, and the draft states that the competitor won a named industry award last year. She can find no record of that award anywhere. What should she do first?
options: A) Establish whether the award claim came from material she supplied or from Claude's general knowledge.
B) Ask Claude whether it is confident about the award before she spends any more time on it.
C) Ask Claude to restate the award claim with more supporting detail so that it becomes easier to check.
D) Delete the sentence about the award and circulate the remainder of the draft to her wider team.
correct_answers: A) Establish whether the award claim came from material she supplied or from Claude's general knowledge.
explanations: Correct. Knowing where a claim originated is what separates a fabrication from a real detail she simply has not located, and it determines every step that follows.
Incorrect. A statement of confidence is generated the same way the claim was, so it adds no independent information about whether the award exists.
Incorrect. Asking for more detail around an unsupported claim usually produces more unsupported detail, which makes the claim harder to dismiss rather than easier to check.
Incorrect. Removing one sentence treats the symptom. If the claim was invented, other statements in the same draft may be too, and she has not yet found out.
